function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something ready‑made, a custom design, or a local specialty: | Type of Order | What You’ll Find | How to Order | |---------------|------------------|--------------| | **Online Delivery Platforms** | • Amazon Fresh, Instacart, Walmart Grocery, Shipt – they partner with local bakeries and deliver fresh cakes on demand.
• Food‑delivery apps like DoorDash, Uber Eats, Postmates, Deliveroo, or SkipTheDishes often have “Bakery” sections. | Search “cake delivery” or “bakery” in the app; filter by “fresh” or “custom.” | | **Specialty Cake Sites** | • **Etsy** – many independent bakers sell custom cakes and can ship them to your address.
• **BakeShare**, **CakeDelivery.com**, **CustomCake.com** – sites dedicated to custom cake design and nationwide shipping. | Browse categories, choose size & flavor, add to cart, and pay online. | | **Local Bakeries & Patisseries** | • Most local bakeries now offer online ordering via their own website or through a simple Google‑Maps “Order Online” link.
• Look for “custom cake” or “birthday cake” in the menu. | Visit the bakery’s site, fill out the order form, or call to confirm details. | | **Grocery Stores & Supermarkets** | • Whole Foods, Kroger, Safeway, Publix, Tesco, Carrefour, etc. – they usually have a bakery section with pre‑made cakes and sometimes custom options. | Order online through the store’s website or app; pick up in‑store or schedule delivery. | | **Specialty Dessert Shops** | • **Ladurée**, **Pierre Hermé**, **Baker & Spice**, **Magnolia Bakery** – known for high‑quality pastries and custom cakes. | Check each shop’s website for online ordering or call ahead. | | **Catering & Event Services** | • Companies like **Goldbelly**, **CaterCow**, or local catering firms can supply large cakes for events. | Contact the caterer directly; they’ll handle pickup/delivery logistics. | ### Tips for Ordering a Cake 1. **Check Delivery Times** – Many platforms let you choose a specific delivery window (e.g., “next‑day morning”). 2. **Read Reviews** – Especially for custom orders, look at photos and ratings from previous customers. 3. **Confirm Ingredients** – If you have allergies or dietary restrictions, double‑check the ingredient list or ask the baker directly. 4. **Ask About Shipping Fees** – Some sites charge extra for delivery outside a certain radius. 5. **Track Your Order** – Most platforms provide real‑time tracking once the cake leaves the bakery. If you tell me your city or zip code, I can narrow down the best local options for you!
